stories.title_en: Posing as Daoists to Swindle the Salt Censor

paragraphs.zh: 唐寅，字伯虎，又字子畏，南京吴趋里人也。中弘治戊午南京解元，因事被黜之。后遂放浪不羁，流留花酒。善诗文，画极工。与文征明、文征仲、祝希哲等为友，皆极一时之名流也。日游平康妓家，滑稽为乐，随口成文。有一皂隶，携纸一张求画。伯虎援笔，画螺蛳十餘个，题诗于上云：“不是蝤蛑不是蛏，海味之中少此名。千呼万呼呼不出，只待人来打窟臀。”众皆大笑。偶一日出，见县前枷一和尚。众人请曰：“可将此和尚作诗一首。”伯虎询知和尚被枷缘由，援笔题于枷上曰：“皂隶官差去采茶，不要纹银只要赊。县里捉来三十板，方盘托出大西瓜。”知县送客出来见之，问是何人所作，或以伯虎对，即将和尚释之。其捷于口才，大约类此。
paragraphs.en: Tang Yin, courtesy name Bohu, also Ziwei, was from Wuqu Lane in Nanjing. He placed first in the Hongzhi wuwu (1498) Nanjing provincial examination, then lost his degree over a scandal. After that he lived without restraint, lingering among flowers and wine. He was skilled at poetry and prose, and especially at painting. He was friends with Wen Zhengming, Wen Zhengzhong, Zhu Xizhe, and others—all famous men of that generation. Day after day he visited the pleasure houses, making jokes for fun and composing as soon as his mouth opened. A yamen runner once brought a sheet of paper and asked for a painting. Bohu took up the brush, painted a dozen or so snails, and wrote on it: “Not a swimming crab, not a razor clam; among seafood this one barely has a name. Call a thousand times, ten thousand times, it will not come out; it only waits for someone to smack its hole-rump.” Everyone laughed hard. One day he went out and saw a monk in a cangue in front of the county yamen. People asked him to make a poem on the monk. Bohu asked why the monk had been cangued, then wrote on the cangue: “The runner, sent on official business, went to pick tea; he wanted no fine silver, only goods on credit. The county seized him for thirty strokes; on a square tray they served up a big watermelon.” The magistrate, seeing guests out, noticed it, asked who had written it, was told it was Bohu, and promptly released the monk. His ready tongue was generally of this kind.

paragraphs.zh: 一日，与祝希哲等十数辈，携装游维扬，日与妓者饮酒，声色为乐。将及一月，资用殆尽。希哲曰：“黄金用尽，作何计策乎？”伯虎曰：“无妨！当今盐使者，资财巨万。我和你二人，可假扮女贞观道士以化之。”二人即扮道士。值盐使者升堂，二人俯伏阶下，云：“女贞观道士参见。”盐使者大怒曰：“岂不闻御史台风霜凛凛耶？是何道者，敢此无状！”将挞之。二人徐对曰：“明公以小道为游方觅食者耶？小道遍游天下，所交者皆极海内名流。即如吴邑唐伯虎、文征明、祝希哲辈，无不与小道折节为友。凡诗词歌赋，应口辄成。明公如不信，愿奏薄技，惟明公所命。”盐使者乃指堂下石牛为题，命二人联诗一首。伯虎应声即吟云：“嵯峨怪石倚云边，”哲云：“抛掷于今定几年。”虎云：“台藓作毛因雨长，”哲云：“藤萝穿鼻任风牵。”虎云：“从来不食溪边草，”哲云：“自古难耕陇上田。”虎云：“怪杀牧童鞭不起，”哲云：“笛声斜挂夕阳烟。”
paragraphs.en: One day, with Zhu Xizhe and a dozen others, he packed up and traveled to Weiyang. Day after day they drank with courtesans and made music and beauty their pleasure. After nearly a month their money was almost gone. Xizhe said, “The gold is spent—what’s the plan?” Bohu said, “No matter. The Salt Censor these days is worth tens of thousands. You and I can pose as Daoist priests of Nüzhen Abbey and tap him for it.” The two dressed as Daoists. When the Salt Censor held court they knelt at the foot of the steps and said, “Daoist priests of Nüzhen Abbey present themselves.” The Salt Censor was furious: “Have you not heard that an inspector’s court is frost and wind? What kind of Daoists dare this insolence!” He was about to have them beaten. The two answered calmly: “Does Your Honor take us for wandering priests begging meals? We have traveled the whole empire; those we keep company with are all famous men within the seas. Even Tang Bohu, Wen Zhengming, and Zhu Xizhe of Wu county treat us as friends without standing on rank. Poetry, lyrics, songs, rhapsodies—we finish them as soon as the mouth opens. If Your Honor does not believe us, we offer a small sample; command us as you please.” The Salt Censor pointed to a stone ox below the hall and ordered them to compose a linked verse. Bohu answered at once: “A towering strange rock leans against the clouds.” Zhe: “Thrown down—who can tell how many years by now.” Hu: “Moss on the terrace makes its hair, grown by the rain.” Zhe: “Vines thread its nose, left for the wind to tug.” Hu: “It has never eaten grass beside the stream.” Zhe: “From of old it could never plow the ridge fields.” Hu: “No wonder the herdboy’s whip cannot raise it.” Zhe: “His flute hangs aslant in the sunset haze.”

paragraphs.zh: 盐使者览毕，霁色问曰：“诗则佳矣。将欲何为？”二人曰：“顷者女贞观圮坏。闻明公宽仁好施，愿捐俸金修葺，以成胜事，亦且不朽。”盐使者大悦，即檄吴兴二县，可给库银五百与之。二人见盐使者应允，速夜赴吴兴，假为道士说关节行状，对吴兴二县云：“今有盐使者修葺女贞观，此系盛举，可依数与之，不可宽缓。”吴兴二县果如数与之。二人得银大悦，曰：“不将万丈深潭计，安得骊龙项下珠？”复往维扬，聚交游十数辈，于妓者家欢呼剧饮，纵其所乐。不十数日，五百之金费用殆尽。后盐使者按临吴兴，束衣冠往女贞观，则见其倾圯如故。召吴兴二县责之，二县对曰：“日前唐伯虎与祝希哲从维扬来，极称明公兴此盛举，小知县即依数与之矣。”盐使者怅然，知为二人所骗，但惜其才，故亦不究。
paragraphs.en: The Salt Censor finished reading, his face softened, and he asked, “The poem is fine. What do you want?” The two said, “Nüzhen Abbey has lately fallen into ruin. We hear Your Honor is generous and fond of giving. If you would donate salary to repair it, it would complete a worthy deed, and the merit would not fade.” The Salt Censor was delighted and issued a directive to the two counties of Wuxing: issue five hundred taels from the treasury to them. Seeing that he had agreed, the two hurried that very night to Wuxing, posed as Daoists carrying the Censor’s instructions, and told the two counties: “The Salt Censor is repairing Nüzhen Abbey. This is a grand undertaking. Give the sum as ordered; do not delay.” The two counties paid it in full. The two men, delighted with the silver, said, “If we had not reckoned on the ten-thousand-fathom pool, how would we have got the pearl under the black dragon’s chin?” They went back to Weiyang, gathered their dozen companions, shouted and drank in the courtesans’ houses, and did as they pleased. In fewer than ten days the five hundred taels were gone. Later the Salt Censor toured Wuxing, put on his robes and cap, and went to Nüzhen Abbey—only to find it still in ruins as before. He summoned the two counties and rebuked them. They answered, “The other day Tang Bohu and Zhu Xizhe came from Weiyang and praised Your Honor for raising this grand work; we magistrates paid the sum as ordered.” The Salt Censor was dismayed, knew he had been taken in by the two men, but valued their talent, so he did not pursue it.

paragraphs.zh: 按：唐伯虎、祝希哲，皆海内一时名家也。但以不得志于时，遂纵于声色，青楼酒肆中，无不闻其名。然非口若悬河，才高倚马，何以能倾动使院？此之骗，可谓骗之善矣。独计当今冠进贤而坐虎皮者，咸思削民脂以润私橐，敛众怨以肥身家，其所以骗民者何如！乃一旦反为唐、祝所骗，亦可为贪墨者一儆。但其知而不究，亦可谓有怜才之心者矣。
paragraphs.en: Note: Tang Bohu and Zhu Xizhe were both famous men of their generation within the seas. Blocked in their careers, they gave themselves to music and beauty; there was no brothel or wineshop that had not heard their names. Yet without tongues like rivers in flood and talent that could draft as fast as a horse can run, how could they have shaken the Censor’s yamen? This swindle may be called a swindle well done. Consider today’s men in the “worthy-and-good” cap, sitting on tiger skins: they all think of scraping the people’s fat to grease their private bags, gathering the crowd’s resentment to fatten their households—and how they swindle the people! Then one day they themselves are swindled by Tang and Zhu, which may serve as a warning to the greedy. That the Censor knew and still did not prosecute may also be called a heart that pities talent.

stories.title_en: Chen Quan’s Scheme to Sleep with a Famous Courtesan

paragraphs.zh: 金陵陈全者，百万巨富也。其为人风流潇洒，尤善滑稽。凡见一物，能速成口号。尝与本地院妓往来，唯一妓最得意。夏间瓜初出，院妓将瓜皮二片，放于门限内，诈令一人慌忙叫全云：“某姐姐偶得危病，要你一相见方瞑目。”全即乘马速至，慌忙进门，脚踹瓜皮跌倒。众妓鼓掌大笑云：“陈官人快做一口号，不得迟！”全即答曰：“陈全走得忙，院子安排定。只因两块皮，几丧我的命。”众妓欣然，遂会饮而罢。
paragraphs.en: Chen Quan of Jinling was a man of enormous wealth. He was easy in manner and especially good at jokes. Whatever he saw, he could turn into a doggerel verse at once. He used to go back and forth with the local registered courtesans; one of them was his particular favorite. In summer, when the first melons came out, the house put two pieces of melon rind just inside the threshold and sent someone running to shout to Quan: “Sister So-and-so has suddenly taken a mortal illness; she wants to see you once before she closes her eyes.” Quan mounted at once and rode hard. He rushed in, stepped on the rind, and fell. The courtesans clapped and laughed: “Master Chen, make a verse at once—no delay!” Quan answered: “Chen Quan came in a rush; the house had it all arranged. Just because of two pieces of rind, I nearly lost my life.” The women were pleased, and they drank together and left it at that.

paragraphs.zh: 又一日，与众妓游湖，见新造一船。众妓云：“速作一口号，勿迟！”全即答曰：“新造船儿一只，当初拟采红莲。于今反作渡头船，来往千千万万。有钱接他上渡，无钱丢在一边。上湿下漏未曾干，隔岸郎君又唤。”众妓皆欢然叹服。凡游戏口号，类如此。
paragraphs.en: Another day he was out on the lake with several courtesans and saw a newly built boat. They said, “Make a verse at once—don’t lag!” Quan answered: “A brand-new little boat; it was meant at first to pick red lotuses. Now it is a ferry at the crossing, coming and going by the thousands. Those with money are taken aboard; those without are tossed aside. Wet above, leaking below, never dry—and from the far bank another gentleman is calling.” The courtesans all laughed and admired him. His joking verses were generally of this kind.

paragraphs.zh: 彼时，浙江杭州有一名妓，号花不如。姿态甚佳，且琴棋诗画，无不通晓。但身价颇高，不与庸俗往来，唯与豪俊交接。每宿一夜，费银六七两方得。全闻之，欲嫖此妓，因而骗之。故令十餘家丁，陆续运船到杭，彼与二三家丁先往。到花不如家，即令家人扛抬皮箱一个———下面俱系纸包砖石，上面一重，俱是纸包真银，每十两为一封———入花不如卧房内，当面开箱取银，赏赐妓家诸役甚厚，奉不如白金十两。不如与众役俱大欢喜，以为此大财主也，所得必不资矣。不如问曰：“客官贵处？”全曰：“金陵。”又问曰：“高姓？”答曰：“姓浪。”又问曰：“尊号？”答曰：“子遂。”不如整盛席相款。子遂不去，只在彼家。过两日，又一家人来报云：“某号船已到。”子遂云：“餘货只放船内，但扛抬皮箱进姐姐家来。”如是者三四次，皮箱有五六个在不如卧房内矣。子遂见不如带珠，云：“你这珠俱不好。我有大珠数百颗，个个俱圆，候此号船到，我去取与你。”
paragraphs.en: At that time Hangzhou in Zhejiang had a famous courtesan called Hua Buru. Her looks were excellent, and she was versed in qin, chess, poetry, and painting. But her price was high. She did not mix with ordinary men, only with the rich and distinguished. A night with her cost six or seven taels. Quan heard of her and wanted to sleep with her, so he set out to swindle her. He had a dozen or more household men send boats on to Hangzhou one after another, while he and two or three servants went first. At Hua Buru’s house he had a leather chest carried in—the bottom layers all paper packets of brick and stone; the top layer all paper packets of real silver, ten taels to a packet—into Hua Buru’s bedroom. In front of everyone he opened the chest, took out silver, tipped the house servants very generously, and presented Buru with ten taels of white silver. Buru and the servants were all delighted, thinking this was a great rich man and that what they would get would be beyond counting. Buru asked, “Where is the guest from?” Quan said, “Jinling.” “Your surname?” “Lang.” “Your courtesy name?” “Zisui.” Buru laid a rich feast. Zisui did not leave; he stayed in her house. After two days another servant came to report: “Boat number such-and-such has arrived.” Zisui said, “Leave the other goods on the boat; just carry the leather chests into Sister’s house.” This happened three or four times, until five or six chests were in Buru’s bedroom. Zisui saw Buru wearing pearls and said, “These pearls of yours are all poor. I have several hundred large pearls, every one round. When this next boat arrives I will fetch them for you.”

paragraphs.zh: 将及月餘，子遂欲心已足。有一家人来报云：“某号船到。”子遂对不如言曰：“此号船不比前船，俱是实落宝货，须我自去一看，兼取大珠与你。其皮箱数个，安顿在你卧房，你须照管，我午后方能进来。但叫你家丁一人，并头口一个，同我去。”不如遂令一人跟随，并驴仔一个，与子遂同去。
paragraphs.en: After more than a month Zisui’s desire was satisfied. A servant came to report: “Boat number such-and-such has arrived.” Zisui said to Buru, “This boat is not like the earlier ones. It is all solid treasure. I must go look myself, and fetch the large pearls for you as well. The several leather chests are in your bedroom; you must watch them. I cannot come back until afternoon. Just send one of your men and one mount with me.” Buru sent a man and a donkey to go with Zisui.

paragraphs.zh: 行至半路，子遂慌忙言曰：“我钥匙一把，安放在你姐姐房内，一时起身，未及带来，你要去取来。”其人即回取。子遂云：“且止！要有我亲手字去，你姐姐方肯把钥匙交付与你。不然，取不来。”子遂乃下驴入纸店，写一口号云：“杭州花不如，接着金台浪子遂，着了人，赔了驴。从今别后，哪得明珠？”封识与那人回。不如开封视之，知被骗矣。忙开皮箱一看，俱系砖石。子遂预令家人买舟俟候，一到河边，即上舟回京。后不如细访，亦知是南京陈全，然已无如之何矣。
paragraphs.en: Halfway there Zisui said in a hurry, “I left a key in your sister’s room. I got up in a rush and did not bring it. You must go back and fetch it.” The man turned to go. Zisui said, “Wait! You will need a note in my own hand, or your sister will not give you the key. Otherwise you will not get it.” Zisui got off the donkey, went into a paper shop, and wrote a verse: “Hangzhou’s Hua Buru took in Jintai’s Lang Zisui; she was taken in, and she paid a donkey. From this parting on, where will she get bright pearls?” He sealed it and sent the man back. Buru opened it, saw she had been swindled, and hurriedly opened the chests—all brick and stone. Zisui had already told his men to hire a boat and wait; as soon as he reached the river he boarded and went back to the capital. Later Buru inquired carefully and learned it was Chen Quan of Nanjing, but there was nothing she could do.

paragraphs.zh: 按：妓家尝是骗人，轻者丧家，重者丧身，未尝有被人骗者；况花不如高抬身价，选拣孤老，其骗人财尤难计算。岂知有陈全之术，又有神出鬼没者乎！赔人赔驴，悔无及矣。此虽陈全之不羁，亦足供笼络院之一笑云。
paragraphs.en: Note: Brothels are used to swindling people. The lighter cases ruin a household; the heavier ones cost a life. One rarely hears of them being swindled themselves. Hua Buru, moreover, put her price high and picked her patrons; the wealth she took from men is past counting. Who would have thought Chen Quan had a method still more like spirits coming and going? She lost a man and a donkey, and regret came too late. This was Chen Quan’s lack of restraint, yet it is also good for a laugh at how the pleasure houses can be played.
